text: Boyd's homeostatic property cluster (HPC) theory of natural kinds differs from Kripke-Putnam essentialism chiefly in that HPC:
choices: denies that there are any natural kinds, treating all classification as merely conventional.
holds that kind membership requires a single microstructural essence shared by every member.
locates kind membership in a cluster of co-occurring properties sustained by an underlying homeostatic mechanism, with no single property necessary and sufficient for membership.
applies only to chemical kinds such as water and gold, and not to biological species.
explanation: Boyd's HPC theory replaces a single defining essence with a cluster of properties held together by a homeostatic mechanism, allowing variation and borderline cases—which is why it fits biological species that lack microstructural essences. Distractor 1 states Kripke-Putnam essentialism (water is necessarily H2O), the view HPC is designed to avoid, and distractor 3 reverses HPC's central application, since it was developed precisely for species.
